tldr: A controlled experiment found that software developers using GitHub Copilot completed a JavaScript HTTP server task 55.8% faster than those without it, with the largest gains among less experienced, older, and heavier-coding developers.
contributions: First controlled experiment measuring productivity impacts of AI tools in professional software development
Evidence of statistically significant 55.8% reduction in task completion time with Copilot (95% CI: 21%-89%)
Identification of heterogeneous treatment effects showing greater benefits for novice, older, and high-volume programmers
methods: The researchers conducted a controlled experiment between May 15 and June 20, 2022, recruiting 95 professional programmers via Upwork. Participants were randomized into a treated group (n=45) with access to GitHub Copilot and a control group (n=50) without it. Both groups were tasked with implementing an HTTP server in JavaScript as quickly as possible, with unconstrained access to internet search and Stack Overflow. Task completion time was measured via GitHub Classroom test suites (12 correctness checks), and heterogeneous effects were analyzed using Horvitz-Thomson transformation followed by regression on covariates.
results: Of 95 developers randomized, 35 from each group completed the task and survey. The treated group averaged 71.17 minutes versus 160.89 minutes for the control group, a 55.8% reduction (p=0.0017, 95% CI: [21%, 89%]). The treated group's success rate was 7 percentage points higher but not statistically significant (95% CI: [-0.11, 0.25]). Less experienced developers, those coding more hours per day, and developers aged 25-44 benefited most. Self-reported productivity gains averaged 35% in both groups, underestimating the actual 55.8% gain. Willingness-to-pay (irrelevant price) was $27.25/month for the treated group vs $16.91/month for control, significantly different at the 95% level.
limitations: Study examined only a standardized programming task, not collaborative work on large projects in professional or open-source settings
Productivity benefits may vary across specific tasks and programming languages, limiting generalizability
The study did not examine effects of AI on code quality, which has performance and security implications
Participants were relatively lower-income (median $10,000-$19,000/year) and predominantly from India and Pakistan, limiting demographic generalizability
The sample size of 35 completers per group is modest
